## Claims
- [source-backed] \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) has integral Schur basis \(\{\bar s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\), and \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution preserving Littlewood–Richardson multiplication under conjugation. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218; 263-269; 481-485]
- [computed] For the conjugate non-self-conjugate inputs \([222,4^5]\subseteq\Lambda/I_{5,4}\) and \([33,5^4]\subseteq\Lambda/I_{4,5}\), complete \(A_+J\)-relation matrices and quotient Smith data in degrees \(6,\ldots,20\) agree: free-rank sequence \((1,1,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0)\) and no torsion in either case. [artifact 5b6e59b74af1b386568e8d3014cdef276ec80f89225cf5ba2367c73fa3b0a993]
- [proved] Conditional on the accepted ideal correspondence \(\omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}\), conjugation induces a graded integral isomorphism
  \[
  J_v/A_+J_v\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;J_{v^\vee}/A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee}.
  \]
  Consequently it preserves every degreewise torsion subgroup and free rank.

## Strategy
Put \(q=n-r\),
\[
A=\Lambda/I_{r,q},\qquad A^\vee=\Lambda/I_{q,r},
\]
and grade by partition weight.  Since
\[
\lambda\nsubseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\nsubseteq r^q,
\]
\(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) descends to a graded integral ring isomorphism
\[
\bar\omega:A\xrightarrow{\sim}A^\vee.
\]
It preserves weight because \(|\lambda'|=|\lambda|\).  Hence
\[
\bar\omega(A_+)=A^\vee_+,
\]
where \(A_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d\), independently of presentations such as \((h_1,\ldots,h_q)\).

Assume the accepted ideal correspondence
\[
\bar\omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}.
\]
Then
\[
\bar\omega(A_+J_v)
 =\bar\omega(A_+)\bar\omega(J_v)
 =A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee}.
\]
Therefore \(\bar\omega|_{J_v}\) descends to the displayed quotient isomorphism.  Its degree-\(d\) restriction is an integral abelian-group isomorphism, so
\[
\operatorname{Tor}(Q_d)\cong\operatorname{Tor}(Q^\vee_d),
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}Q_d=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}Q^\vee_d.
\]
This includes \(a=0\), zero degree pieces, and all degrees outside the finite ambient boxes. Cohomological grading is also preserved after doubling partition weight.

The required quotient-level computation dependency is accepted artifact `5b6e59b74af1b386568e8d3014cdef276ec80f89225cf5ba2367c73fa3b0a993`: exit status \(0\); executable-script SHA-256 `a53b2b65248a952119b244db2f383be666904ceb71b2225e71ebd8dcb46cb5a5`; inputs
\[
([2,2,2,0,0],[4,4,4,4,4],\{1,2,3,4\}),
\quad
([3,3,0,0],[5,5,5,5],\{1,2,3,4,5\}),
\]
with degrees \(6,\ldots,20\). Its persisted output contains the ordered bases, complete Pieri relation matrices, Smith data, quotient ranks, torsion lists, and comparison.

## Gaps
The isomorphism is conditional on the accepted quotient-conjugation and ideal-correspondence premises; those premises are not reproved here. The finite computation corroborates only its stated inputs and does not prove the all-parameter result. No parent theorem is claimed.
